title: Tool formatter and slash-command presentation contracts
objective: Give every production tool family and registered slash command a stable semantic lifecycle contract without inferring business outcomes from prose.
requirements: All 41 production tool names, aliases, dynamic MCP names, and unknown fallback are covered.
Queued, running, success, warning, failure, inspect, and full states are tested for every production formatter.
All 24 registered slash commands have typed family/action/target/display/risk/outcome contracts.
Legacy OnEvent text remains byte-compatible while typed results are bounded, ANSI-free, redacted, and explicitly marked when they mirror the legacy stream.
Text-returning commands report explicit success, warning, partial, failure, denial, cancellation, timeout, interruption, or exit through a domain result channel.
Every production tool has a fixture matching its actual structured wire shape rather than a generic success map.
write_scope: tui tool formatter and commands presentation adapter

acceptance.criterion: Production formatter catalog has 41 exact entries plus aliases/dynamic fallback.
Every formatter covers the complete lifecycle and expansion matrix.
Every production tool exposes tool-specific fields from a realistic structured result.
24 registered slash commands use exact presentation contracts.
Typed command outcomes, sections, and evidence references survive without replaying mirrored legacy text.
Legacy text is unchanged and domain failures are explicit, not parsed.
Secrets, auth tokens, device codes, ANSI, and long output are safe and bounded.

remaining_risks: A newly registered tool or slash command must extend the catalog test or intentionally accept the conservative fallback.

result.summary: Tool and slash-command output is semantic, lifecycle-aware, explicit about business outcomes, and renderer-neutral.
